mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team (Team A) exhibits a high shots-FOR but low shots_on_target-FOR ratio (low conversion accuracy), while the defending team (Team B) allows a relatively low shots_on_target AGAINST rate. In such joint conditions, measure Team A's corner_kicks FOR.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when Team A's shot accuracy is low (many shots, few on target) and Team B suppresses on-target shots, as off-target attempts and blocked shots are more likely to produce corners than goals
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly considered alongside Team B's defensive suppression of shots_on_target AGAINST, to test whether the combined low-accuracy / high-volume-allowed pairing produces a different corner-kick yield than either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for Team A and a separate observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for Team B simultaneously — not reducible to any single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B holds above-average possession (FOR) and simultaneously generates above-average corners FOR. Measure whether Team A's corners AGAINST co-varies with Team B's possession level across this joint distribution, or whether corner generation is decoupled from possession for Team B.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner_kicks FOR rises with possession FOR up to a threshold, but the relationship saturates or decouples at high possession levels, suggesting a non-linear rather than proportional link between possession dominance and corner generation
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team B's corner_kicks FOR (high, rising in recent form) and Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST (also elevated) is tested jointly against Team B's possession FOR, to determine whether Team B's corner dominance is possession-driven or possession-independent.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a non-linear / threshold relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) for the same team, not a simple single-observable band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A holds below-average possession (FOR below competition mean of 50). Within those matches, compare Team A's goals FOR in the first half versus second half. Team A scores markedly more in the second half (0.767) than first half (0.279) overall; test whether this half-skew is amplified or suppressed when possession deficit is larger.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's second-half goals FOR rises relative to first-half goals FOR as Team A's possession deficit deepens, suggesting a counter-attacking or late-game pattern that is more pronounced when possession is ceded
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals FOR split by half (first half vs second half) is tested jointly against Team A's possession deficit (Team A possession FOR is below 50, opponent possession is above 50), to determine whether Team A's scoring pattern is concentrated in a specific half when playing as the lower-possession side.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state split (half-level) conditioned simultaneously on a continuous possession-deficit dimension — requiring both half resolution and a joint second observable, not covered by any single-observable or single-band baseline.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B commits above-average fouls FOR. Within those matches, compare Team B's goals FOR in the first half versus second half, and also measure yellow_cards FOR. Test whether the high-foul regime is associated with a front-loaded goal pattern and elevated card accumulation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In matches where Team B's fouls FOR is elevated, Team B's first-half goals FOR is disproportionately higher relative to second half, and yellow_cards FOR is also elevated — suggesting a joint aggressive-early-dominance regime
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals FOR split by half (first half vs second half) is tested jointly against Team B's fouls FOR, to determine whether Team B's strong first-half scoring (0.806 per match) is associated with a high-foul, physically aggressive style that also generates yellow cards, and whether this joint pattern shifts across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a three-observable joint relationship (goals by half, fouls, yellow_cards) with a within-match half-level split conditioned on a continuous foul-rate dimension — not reducible to any single observable or single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both Team A's fouls FOR and Team B's fouls AGAINST are simultaneously above the competition mean. Within that joint high-foul context, measure cards_2h FOR and AGAINST for both teams. Compare to the baseline cards_2h rate in matches where only one side's foul rate is elevated.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: cards_2h (for both teams combined) rises when both Team A fouls FOR and Team B fouls AGAINST are jointly elevated above competition mean, with the joint condition producing a greater second-half card rate than either team's individual foul elevation alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's fouls FOR and Team B's fouls AGAINST (both elevated relative to competition context) is tested against second-half cards (cards_2h) for both teams, to determine whether a high-mutual-foul-rate match context produces a disproportionate second-half card escalation beyond what each team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for Team A and fouls AGAINST for Team B) simultaneously, tested against a within-match-period outcome (second-half cards) — involving two opponent-descriptor dimensions and a half-level split, not covered by any single-observable baseline.
